designs.title: How Beer Is Made
designs.why: Clean, solid, line-only art with no halftone and no isolated specks. The step headings and captions (caps about 5 mm) are crisp and will hold on a 156–200 mesh. The flow reads clearly from 3 m and the 10% coverage keeps the white underbase soft on the black tee. The only risk is the tightest cross-hatching inside the vessels: about 260 openings are 4 px (0.17 mm) or smaller, and white ink on black will bleed into them and fill them.
designs.fix: Open the densest hatching inside the tanks and kegs to at least 0.25 mm gaps, or knock out the sub-0.2 mm holes, so the white ink doesn't fill in on the black tee.

designs.title: Gin Botanicals
designs.why: A handsome engraving plate with a well-balanced 2-2-1 layout. The halftone is around 39 lpi, which is a sensible, printable ruling for cotton on 230 mesh. The italic Latin names are clean and legible. The highlight dots of 1–4 px (around 13k of them) will drop out, but they sit in light areas, so the loss reads as natural vignetting. The shadows in the angelica and orris roots sit close to plugging.
designs.fix: Set a minimum dot of about 0.2 mm and cap the shadows at about 85% (open the darkest root and peel shading slightly) so dot gain on the white tee doesn't fill the dark areas.

designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: The picture is appealing, but production-wise it is a heavy block: coverage reaches 40–49% across the middle bands and is built mostly from mid-to-dark 39 lpi halftone. On a white cotton tee, dot gain will merge the terraces and vine rows into a muddy grey mass and the print will feel stiff. The foreground grapes and trunks already sit close to solid, while the farmhouse and cypresses, the focal point, are small and get lost in the texture from 3 m.
designs.fix: Pull the midtones and shadows back by about 15–20% (curve the terraces and foreground lighter, keep the solid blacks only for the cypresses and grape clusters). That restores contrast, avoids plugging, and lets the farmhouse read as the focal point.
